title: Median Salary
description:
Report the median salary of the company: the middle value when salaries are sorted, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even. Ignore NULL salaries.

Name the column `median_salary`. The result is exactly one row.
hint: SQLite has no PERCENTILE function. Take 1 or 2 rows from the middle with LIMIT/OFFSET and average them.
outputExplanation: With 8 non-NULL salaries, the median is the average of the 4th and 5th values: $107,500.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Single employee — median is that salary
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'IT','A');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','X',100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Even count (4) — average of two middle values
All NULLs excluded — empty set returns NULL median
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'IT','A');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','X',NULL,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','X',NULL,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Mix of NULLs and values
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'IT','A');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','X',100,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','X',200,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'C','X',NULL,1,1,'2020-01-01');
